raw_response:
I'm 50 this year, been farming these 7 mu for 35 years. Only finished primary school, but I know my land better than any book. It's just me and my wife — our children are working in the city. We do most of the work ourselves because hired labor is 100 yuan a day now and we don't have cash to throw around.

It's late April. My half-mu of spinach that I seeded in early March is ready to cut — should get about 3,000 jin total, good for some early cash and eating. The 2 mu of spring cabbage I planted in March is heading up nice. Next week I'll transplant my chili seedlings — 3 mu, same as last year. The buyer still comes to the village to collect, so I'm not worried about selling. Come June, when the cabbage comes off, I'll put 1.5 mu into summer maize. That's our food security and a little money on the side.

Money is tight. I have about 7,000 yuan for inputs this year. Chili takes the biggest bite — seedlings cost me nearly 300 yuan per mu, plus fertilizer and spraying. I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, that's my base. Then when the chili flowers, I topdress with about half a bag of urea. If the plants look yellow at fruit set, I do another half bag. My neighbor Lao Wang used two full bags of compound on his chili last year and got plenty of peppers, but then the price dropped and he barely made it back. So I stick to what I know — one bag compound, one bag urea split in two.

Cabbage gets less — about 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting, then one topdress of urea when heads start forming. Maize just gets one bag of compound fertilizer at planting and nothing more. Spinach grows fast, just a little compound fertilizer and it's fine.

For water, I have my well but the pump costs electricity. Chili gets watered four times — right after transplanting, at flowering, when fruits set, and once in August if it's dry. Cabbage gets three times. Maize is tough, once or twice is enough. Spinach gets twice while it's small.

I have to spray chili for aphids and disease every year. Cabbage gets herbicide and maybe one insecticide spray. Maize gets herbicide once. Spinach I just weed by hand, it's not worth spraying.

If weather is normal, I expect chili to give about 3,000 jin per mu, cabbage about 8,000 jin, maize 900 jin, spinach 3,000 jin. But you never know — last year was dry and my chili was down maybe 20%. That's why I don't gamble everything on one crop. Maize and spinach are my insurance. I don't try fancy new varieties much. The hybrid chili my neighbor used did well, so I bought the same. Change is risky when you only have 7 mu and two people working it.
